label: late original-phase positions and the <DEL> step (position ramp, before copying)
explanation: Fires late in the original (input) phase and on the <DEL> delimiter step, almost never during copying (3% of mass) and never at t<=1. The firing rate climbs with position (orig_idx 4: 12%, 8: 60%) and with sequence length L (L=9 holds 41% of mass). Within a sequence, activation usually ramps up over the input phase, peaks on the last input token or two, and decays through <DEL> and the first copy output. The predicate (phase<=1)&(t>=5) captures about 87% of activation mass but only about 33% precision: many late-position steps stay silent. Whether it fires depends on content: sequences whose early tokens include q, 2, u, p, g (and s, z at positions 2-3) fire much more often and more strongly, and the top examples start with 2/p/q followed by s/z. A content filter raises F1 only a little (0.52) and costs a lot of recall, so the content dependence looks graded and distributed, not a clean token rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: q, 2, u, p, g, w; least: r, f, j, e) and the third original token (most: s, z, x, l, q, w; least: r, 2, o, j); timing cues that raise it most: t=7, t=8, t=6.
